I've written the script and performed the analysis, Ary. 

The die appears to be **fair**. 

The simulation produced the following distribution across the 6,000 rolls:

| Face | Observed Count |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 1,019 |
| 2 | 965 |
| 3 | 983 |
| 4 | 1,009 |
| 5 | 1,024 |
| 6 | 1,000 |

A Chi-square goodness-of-fit test resulted in a **p-value of 0.7717**. Since this is well above the typical threshold of 0.05, we cannot reject the hypothesis that the die is fair.

The results are stored in `rolls.csv`, and the scripts used are `simulate_die.py` and `analyze_fairness.py`.
